# IBANforge

> Know the bank behind any IBAN: IBAN validation, BIC/SWIFT lookup, Swiss clearing (BC-Nummer / QR-IID / SIX BankMaster — full payment-rail participation, the deepest Swiss clearing data in any public API), EMI/vIBAN classification, SEPA Instant + VoP reachability, and sanctions and compliance risk scoring, for developers and AI agents, by REST or MCP — with x402 micropayments, and an API key that needs no e-mail, no card and no signup.

121k+ BIC entries (39k+ LEI-enriched via GLEIF) · 1,100+ Swiss BC-Nummern (SIX) · 89 countries · 900+ non-bank issuer classifications (EMI, payment institutions, digital banks) — live counts at https://api.ibanforge.com/llms.txt

## Data sources and attribution

GLEIF · SIX BankMaster · SwiftCodes (MIT) · Deutsche Bundesbank · Oesterreichische Nationalbank · Banque nationale de Belgique · Národná banka Slovenska · Central Bank of the Republic of San Marino · Finance Finland · NBP · EBA STEP2 · OFAC · EU · UN · FATF · EPC.
UK deposit-taking authorisation: Bank of England (List of Banks, 2026-08), used with the Bank of England's written permission. The month of the list in force is served live at https://api.ibanforge.com/llms.txt
Slovak bank codes: Národná banka Slovenska, Directory of identification codes for the domestic payment system (version 225, effective 2026-05-18), reproduced under the NBS site terms — the source is named and the file is not altered. The edition in force is served live at https://api.ibanforge.com/llms.txt
San Marino bank codes: Central Bank of the Republic of San Marino, operating banks — four banks, read from the BCSM site. No terms of use are published there, so the licence is recorded as UNKNOWN and the source is credited by choice; the page states no edition, so the credit carries the date we read it. The list names the holder of a code it carries and does NOT publish the allocation of the ABI code space: an absence from it is not a non-allocation. Read date in force served live at https://api.ibanforge.com/llms.txt

## API Base URL
https://api.ibanforge.com

## How AI agents connect (pick one)

### Try it right now, no key, no wallet (REST)
curl -s -X POST https://api.ibanforge.com/v1/iban/validate -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"iban":"CH9300762011623852957"}'
The first 25 calls a day from one IP are served in full, free. The answer carries a `trial` block saying how many are left today and how to take a key that needs no e-mail at all (25 a month, claimable to 200 a month). These 25 are a day, on this route only; the key's 25 are a month, on every route — a different thing, not a bigger one. Past 25 the route answers 402 again, `cause.reason = "trial_exhausted"`. Send a REAL iban: an empty `{}` body is the x402 discovery probe and always gets the 402.

### MCP server (stdio — easiest, no signup)
npx -y ibanforge-mcp
Claude Desktop / Cursor / Cline config:
{"mcpServers": {"ibanforge": {"command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "ibanforge-mcp"]}}}
Optional: set IBANFORGE_API_KEY=ifk_... in env. Get one with no e-mail: POST https://api.ibanforge.com/v1/keys/generate with no body at all (25 req/month), then POST /v1/keys/claim with the key in the Authorization header to raise it to 200 a month.

### MCP server (streamable HTTP — no install)
POST https://api.ibanforge.com/mcp  (JSON-RPC: initialize → tools/list → tools/call)

### OpenAI agents (no Custom GPT or ChatGPT Plus needed)
Agents SDK: point MCPServerStreamableHttp at the MCP URL above — the 11 tools auto-load.
Function-calling (Chat Completions / Responses): wire tools to the OpenAPI at /openapi.json.

### Pay-per-call without an API key (x402, USDC on Base L2)
GET https://api.ibanforge.com/.well-known/x402 returns the full catalog. Any agent with a Base wallet can discover, pay, and call.
Zero to first payment in 3 steps (wallet with budget → USDC on Base → one $5 payment for 1,000 credits): https://ibanforge.com/docs/pay-as-an-agent?src=llms

## 11 MCP tools
- validate_iban — validate one IBAN + enrich (BIC, issuer EMI/vIBAN, SEPA, VoP, risk, Swiss bc_nummer). Cost: $0.005
- batch_validate_iban — up to 100 IBANs in one call. Cost: $0.002 per IBAN (e.g. 100 = $0.20)
- lookup_bic — resolve a BIC/SWIFT into bank, country, city, LEI. Cost: $0.003
- lookup_ch_clearing — Swiss BC-Nummer / IID → institution, address, full rail participation (SIC, euroSIC, CHF instant, LSV+/BDD), QR-IID. The deepest Swiss clearing data in any public API. Cost: $0.003
- check_compliance — sanctions (OFAC, bank-BIC level) + FATF + SEPA Instant + VoP + risk score 0-100. Informational, not regulated AML/CFT. Cost: $0.02
- validate_payment_reference — RF/ISO 11649, Swiss QRR, Belgian OGM/VCS, Finnish viitenumero checksums against the dated document that publishes each rule, plus the QRR/QR-IBAN pairing verdict. Cost: free
- check_postal_address — ISO 20022 postal address against one rail's published rules (sps, hvps_plus, fedwire), one finding per rule with its source and date. Cost: free
- check_swiss_qr_bill — Swiss QR-bill payload check: header, QR-IBAN and reference pairing, checksums, structured (S) versus combined (K) addresses ahead of 14.11.2026, with a proposed structured form. Free.
- send_feedback — report incorrect data or claim an x402 refund, no account. Cost: free
- request_api_key — open a key request a human approves in a browser: no e-mail, no card, no account. Free, and it works even after the daily limit. Cost: free
- poll_api_key — collect the key once a human has approved it, handed over exactly once, with the config line to paste. Cost: free

## REST endpoints
- POST /v1/iban/validate — single IBAN, full enrichment ($0.005; first 25/day per IP free, no key — see the keyless trial above)
- POST /v1/iban/batch — up to 100 IBANs ($0.002 each)
- GET  /v1/bic/{code} — BIC/SWIFT lookup with LEI ($0.003)
- GET  /v1/ch/clearing/{iid} — Swiss clearing lookup ($0.003)
- GET  /v1/gb/firm/{frn} — one UK-regulated firm by Firm Reference Number, from the FCA Financial Services Register: name, status and its date, business type, Companies House number, PSD/EMD status, notices; credited, dated, cached one day ($0.003; answers 503 not_configured, uncharged, on a deployment without the Register API credential)
- POST /v1/iban/compliance — sanctions + FATF + SEPA + VoP + risk ($0.02)
- GET  /v1/iban/format?iban=... — free mod-97 + structure check (no auth)
- GET  /v1/iban/structure[/{country}] — free IBAN templates for 89 countries (no auth)
- GET|POST /v1/reference/validate — free structured payment reference check: RF/ISO 11649, Swiss QRR, Belgian OGM/VCS, Finnish viitenumero (no auth)
- POST /v1/address/check — free ISO 20022 postal address conformity check: sps, hvps_plus, fedwire (no auth)
- GET  /v1/credits/bundles — free, list prepaid credit bundles
- GET  /v1/demo — free example validations
- POST /v1/keys/generate (no body at all) — free API key, no e-mail, no card, 25 req/month
- POST /v1/keys/generate {"email":"you@company.com"} — same route, optional address, and the key is issued already at the full allowance (tier "email", nothing left to claim)
- POST /v1/keys/claim (key in the Authorization header, never the body) — raises that same key to 200 a month with a mailed 6-digit code, or to 200 once with an x402 payment on the key

## How to pay (4 rails, no dead-ends)
- Try before anything: 25 keyless validations/day per IP on POST /v1/iban/validate, and 10 MCP tool calls/day per IP. Tasters, not tiers.
- Free key, nothing asked: POST /v1/keys/generate with no body at all → an ifk_ key, 25 requests a month, on every endpoint. Nothing is mailed and no record is opened.
- Same key, full free allowance: POST /v1/keys/claim with `Authorization: Bearer ifk_...` (never in the body), once the key has served one call. A 6-digit code mailed to an address your human gave you FOR THIS — ask in their words, "Use my address you@company.com to create a free IBANforge key", and never send an address your human has not handed you for this purpose — gives 200 every month; an x402 payment made on the key gives 200 once.
- Credit packs (card or USDC, never expire): 1k = $5, 5k = $20, 25k = $80 → POST /v1/credits/buy/1k|5k|25k
- Pro subscription (card): $29/month for 10,000 requests, resets on the 1st, cancel anytime → https://ibanforge.com/pricing?src=llms
- x402 micropayments: pay per call in USDC on Base L2, no signup

## SDKs
- TypeScript: npm install @ibanforge/sdk
- Python: pip install ibanforge
- Java (17+): com.ibanforge:ibanforge-sdk on Maven Central
- .NET (net8.0): dotnet add package IBANforge.Sdk
